title: Confirming Deactivate saves the edits and shows Part deactivated.
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test with a Sell Price of $20.00.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the part A row.
  2. Replace the Sell Price with 25.00.
  3. Click Inactive under Part Status.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  6. Click the Inactive tab.
  7. Click the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 2:

  • Sell Price shows 25.00.

Step 3:

  • Inactive is selected.

Step 4:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 5:

  • Both windows close, and a green message "Part deactivated." appears and goes away on its own.
  • Part A leaves the Active tab.

Step 6:

  • The Inactive tab lists part A.

Step 7:

  • Sell Price reads 25.00, so the edit was saved, and the title row pill reads "Inactive".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R22: “Confirming saves every change in the dialog, then applies the status, and closes the dialog with "Part deactivated." or "Part activated.".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Part deactivated from the part dialog | "Part deactivated." | Success toast, fades on its own”
